name: Pre-Earnings Long Straddle / Strangle (IV Expansion Buy)
summary: Buy a straddle or strangle days before an earnings date and close it BEFORE the announcement, harvesting the pre-event rise in implied volatility rather than the move itself - the two-sided version the bank was missing alongside its directional earnings entries.

legs.strike_rule: ATM call, delta 0.45-0.55 (straddle); or delta 0.25-0.35 for the cheaper strangle version
legs.dte_rule: first expiry AFTER the earnings date, 14-45 DTE

legs.strike_rule: same strike as the call (straddle), or |delta| 0.25-0.35 (strangle)

max_profit: Bounded in practice by the size of the IV ramp - typically 20-60% of the debit if the trade is exited before the print; unbounded only if held through, which these rules forbid
max_loss: The full debit, and the realistic bad case is a slow bleed as theta outruns the vol ramp
breakevens: Not price-based when traded correctly: the position wins if ATM IV rises more than theta costs over the holding period

greeks.delta: near zero at entry, rehedged or re-centered if it drifts
greeks.theta: negative - the enemy, and the reason the holding window is short
greeks.vega: positive, and the entire source of the intended return

typical_dte: Enter 5-10 trading days before earnings, expiry the first one after the event
when_to_use: Names with a documented pattern of implied volatility rising into the print and a chain liquid enough to exit at a fair price. This is a vega trade, not an event bet - the bank's long-call-into-earnings and long-put-into-earnings entries are the directional versions, and this is the neutral one.
entry_rules: Confirmed earnings date from two sources; if the date is 'estimated', skip the name.
Enter 5-10 trading days before the announcement. Earlier and theta dominates; later and the IV ramp is already paid for.

IV GATE: current ATM IV for the post-earnings expiry must be below the median level it reached in the 2 days before the last 4 announcements. If IV is already at or above that level, there is nothing left to buy.
Debit <= 0.75% of equity per name; at most 3 pre-earnings positions at once and never more than 1 in the same sector.
Prefer the strangle when the straddle debit exceeds the budget, but only when both strikes have OI >= 250.
Both legs same expiry, one MLeg order, no chasing beyond $0.05.
Underlying price >= $30 and average daily option volume >= 1,000 contracts - cheap stocks have chains too coarse to exit.
management_rules: Take profit at 30% gain on the package; the vol ramp rarely pays more than that without the event.
Hard time stop: close by the market close on the day BEFORE the announcement, without exception, profitable or not.
Re-center by rolling to the new ATM strike only if the underlying moves more than 1.5 x ATR(14) and more than 3 days remain before the print; otherwise close.
Never hold through the print. Holding converts a vega trade into an event bet with a guaranteed IV crush working against both legs.
exit_rules: MANDATORY: flat before the announcement. For a post-close reporter, flat by 15:45 ET that day; for a pre-open reporter, flat by 15:45 ET the prior session.
No leg may be held into the event 'because it is cheap' - a residual long leg is a lottery ticket funded by a failed thesis.
Close, never exercise, any ITM long leg.
If the earnings date moves, re-evaluate from scratch: either exit or reset the window.
assignment_risk: None - both legs are long. The only stock-delivery path is auto-exercise of an ITM long leg at expiry, which cannot occur because the position is always closed before the event, well ahead of expiry.
liquidity_needs: Liquid single-name chains; the exit is the hard part, and it happens on the busiest possible day for that name's options.
common_mistakes: Holding through the print and eating the IV crush on both legs; entering when IV has already ramped; buying the weekly expiry that includes the event at the widest spreads of the cycle; treating a gain from an underlying move as evidence the vega thesis worked.
zero_dte_notes: Not appropriate - the trade is explicitly about the days before the event.
family: Completeness gap-fill (cross-family): ratio/naked-financed put and call structures, quantity-unbalanced condors and strangles, stock+option overlays and monetizations, capital-protection and hybrid builds, 0DTE four-leg income, volatility-surface and relative-value trades, event-driven overlays, and roll/adjustment structures
